source.title: Iran-related Designations; Cuba Designation; Issuance of New and Amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions

summary: OFAC announced 'Operation Economic Outcast,' adding 16 Iran-connected individuals and 10 Iran-linked entities to the SDN List under E.O. 13902, plus Cuba's state-owned Banco Internacional de Comercio S.A. (BICSA) under E.O. 14404. The Iran designations target a cluster of recently-formed Iranian 'exchange' and partnership companies registered as 'Other monetary intermediation' businesses in Qeshm, Kish and Tehran, several Iranian and Iraqi banks, a Hong Kong trading company, and individuals linked to these entities, framed by Treasury as action against Iran's international financial networks and shadow-banking architecture. OFAC also issued Russia-related General Licenses 128D and 130B (Lukoil-related wind-downs), Iran-related General License FF (wind-down of transactions with International Development Bank for Investment and Finance), and new/amended FAQs 1276 (Cuba) and 1225 (Russia).

extraction_notes: This is a raw OFAC SDN-list update notice, not a narrative typology report: the SAN004 Front Companies link rests on the structural pattern of the designations (multiple newly-formed 'Other monetary intermediation' exchange/partnership companies tied to designated individuals) rather than an explicit description of the mechanism, hence medium rather than high confidence. None of the 28 named actors (16 individuals, 12 entities including Farab Soroush Afagh Qeshm Company, which is referenced as a Linked-To party but is not itself in this notice's list of newly added entities) resolved against the governed actor register -- all resolve_actor calls returned 'Unresolved', so no actor_id mappings are recorded; a human reviewer should check these against the register separately. Lukoil entities referenced in connection with GL 128D/130B are not designations in this document (they are the subject of authorizing general licenses) and were not extracted as actors. The Iranian Arabic-script name variants given in the source for each individual/entity were omitted from citation quotes per instruction to avoid non-Latin spans; the Latin-script biographic fields were cited instead. The BICSA (Cuba) designation and the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance (Iraq) designation do not independently support a distinct typology beyond SAN004/general sanctions-list activity on the evidence given, and are recorded as actors only.
